sections.title: Medieval France: From Paris to Jerusalem
sections.description: France arguably became France in the thirteenth century. Kings expanded their land from a modest lordship around Paris to the geography we recognize today, they developed the machinery of law and justice while working to root out corruption, Gothic cathedrals reshaped urban skylines, universities revolutionized learning, religious diversity and cultural encounter shaped and tested society, fairs prospered while merchants linked continents, and vernacular literature told tales of love and adventure while making fun of naughty priests. At the same time, France was not purely shaped or contained by its borders. In this seminar, students will trace the making of France in the streets of Paris and fairs of Champagne and also follow knights, clerics, merchants, pilgrims and crusaders as they went outward — to Jerusalem, to Acre, to Constantinople, to Tunis, to Mongol territory — in the interest of trade, crusade and diplomatic relations. Through eyewitness accounts, chronicles, courtly literature, administrative records, architecture, illuminated manuscripts, and material culture, we will reconstruct how medieval people argued, governed, fought, expressed their faith, traded, traveled, and imagined their world, one both familiar and surprising.
